articles.title: [Vantage Point] The Legarda-Leviste solar empire: Who opened the doors?
articles.summary: Vantage Point examines the Anti-Money Laundering Council's allegations concerning Senator Loren Legarda, former Energy secretary Alfonso Cusi, and Congressman Leando Leviste in the acquisition and…

blocks.text: The AMLC’s investigation into renewable-energy contract awards, a sprawling corporate network, and billions in financial transactions raises pressing questions about political influence, regulatory discretion, and private wealth.
On August 22, 2017, the Department of Energy (DOE) during the Rodrigo Duterte administration took two contradictory actions that defy conventional regulatory logic.

On the exact same day, the DOE threatened to cancel a Leviste company’s solar contract for failing to deliver—yet awarded brand-new solar contracts to other Leviste-linked firms. Despite facing default, the developer was handed an even bigger share of the country’s renewable energy projects

That same year, according to the findings by the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC), P170.32 million in cash deposits entered the bank accounts of then-Energy secretary Alfonso Cusi. By 2022, his final year in office, Cusi’s annual cash deposits had climbed to P195.25 million. (READ: Cusi is sole billionaire in Duterte Cabinet at end of 2021)

The AMLC identified 243 cash deposits amounting to P434.85 million during his tenure—with 84.1% of the deposit value concentrated in 2017 and 2022. Whether any link exists between those cash inflows and the energy contracts remains an evidentiary issue that investigators must resolve. (READ: Duterte’s wealth remains secret until the end of his term)
Nearly a decade after those controversial awards, the AMLC’s reported allegations extend beyond Batangas Representative Leandro Leviste to his mother, Senator Loren Legarda, alongside Cusi.

According to reported Court of Appeals records, investigators allege that the three acted in concert to facilitate the acquisition, retention, and transfer of exclusive solar development rights to Leviste-linked corporations.

For more than a year, Vantage Point (see links below this paragraph) has examined how state-awarded development rights formed the bedrock of a multibillion-peso corporate empire. The latest disclosures examine the individuals who helped assemble those corporate vehicles and the public officials whose decisions enabled their expansion.

items: [Vantage Point] The Leviste gambit: Monetizing clean energy for political gains?
[Vantage Point] The solar tale: Jurisprudence slays Leviste’s thinly veiled tact
[Vantage Point] The Leviste solar saga – why markets should be worried
[Vantage Point] Consumers pay for DOE’s delayed action on Leviste firms
[Vantage Point] The Leviste sting: The risks of trading farmland for megawatts
[Vantage Point] As Leandro Leviste cashes out of SPNEC, his private companies remain at the table

blocks.text: Between 2013 and 2021, Leviste reportedly incorporated 35 companies, many sharing the same incorporators and shareholders. Among the recurring names flagged by the AMLC were Legarda’s relatives, former Senate staffers, and even her former nanny.
Figure 1. Recurring names in Leviste’s corporate network

blocks.caption: Source: Reported AMLC findings in Court of Appeals records. Appearances are not ownership percentages or proof of wrongdoing.

blocks.text: Were these individuals beneficial owners risking their own capital, or were they holding shares under arrangements benefiting someone else? Who supplied the equity, exercised effective control, and reaped the financial rewards? AMLC’s allegation of coordinated intervention warrants a rigorous examination of those relationships.

Cusi, meanwhile, faces questions about his role in regulatory approvals. Reported court records state that he personally approved and signed solar energy service contracts for Leviste-associated firms, including awards granted despite alleged defaults on prior commitments. What technical assessments, financial vetting, and compliance reports justified those approvals? Were competing developers held to the same standard?

An exclusive solar service contract reserves a geographic development opportunity, generally barring rival investors from developing the covered area. Granting those exclusive rights to entities unable to deliver can deprive the economy of investments and much-needed generating capacity. According to the AMLC, the 26 contracts which were eventually terminated carried roughly P10.44 billion in unfulfilled obligations. (READ: Duterte approves franchise for solar firm of Loren Legarda’s son)

The financial trail surrounding Cusi extends well beyond cash deposits. Investigators reportedly flagged 735 financial transactions totaling P11.05 billion during his term, spanning inter-account transfers, checks, fiduciary placements and withdrawals, investments, and cash deposits. Transaction volume is not necessarily income or illicit proceeds, but the origins and counterparties demand inspection.
Figure 2. Cusi’s reported cash deposits: P434.85 million

blocks.caption: Source: Reported AMLC findings. 2017 and 2022 account for 84.1% of deposit value; no source of funds is established by this chart.

blocks.text: Investigators also noted substantial activity in Cusi’s accounts after he left public office, coinciding with Leviste’s sale of major shareholdings in SP New Energy Corp. (SPNEC). The reported contract approvals and subsequent financial activity necessitate a thorough review of banking and government records.

Cusi has challenged the accuracy of the Court of Appeals freeze order, categorically denying that he maintained a joint bank account with Golden Sun 999 Realty and Development Corp. He claims the same account number appears twice in the document, with the second entry identifying the correct account holders. The AMLC must address this alleged error and determine whether it affects its financial findings. His denial, however, does not by itself resolve the broader questions surrounding his reported P11.05 billion in financial transactions and the award of solar development contracts to Leviste-associated companies.

Leviste’s widely celebrated entrepreneurial rise merits scrutiny. Beneath the narrative of clean-energy innovation lay a corporate strategy that transformed government-granted development rights into lucrative commercial assets before some projects delivered electricity.
As early as January 2026, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla was examining whether Leviste’s corporate maneuvers circumvented statutory restrictions governing the transfer of congressional franchises.

Although congressional franchises and DOE service contracts are legally distinct instruments, the reported AMLC findings give urgency to that inquiry. Leviste-linked firms accumulated exclusive development rights, consolidated project stakes into the publicly listed SPNEC, and leveraged institutional investments that allowed early shareholders to monetize their positions. (READ: Leandro Leviste sells another P3 billion in SPNEC shares as solar controversies mount)

Across Leviste’s own accounts, the AMLC reportedly traced P57.89 billion in cumulative financial transactions. Investigators separately identified 1,044 checks worth roughly P14.99 billion issued to him by his solar companies, prompting the AMLC to flag potential commingling of personal and corporate funds. Gross transaction totals do not establish personal profit or unlawful enrichment, but they do justify accounting reconciliation.

Leviste maintains that his business dealings were lawful and conducted in the ordinary course of business. Cusi has declined further comment, citing pending court proceedings, while PDP-Laban has dismissed the probe as politically motivated. Yet the DOE’s reported termination notices and payment demands date back to December 2024—predating the flood-control controversy cited in claims of political persecution.

blocks.caption: Leviste denies he made money from selling franchise to Pangilinan’s Meralco group

blocks.text: The Court of Appeals’ freeze orders remain provisional safeguards, not judicial convictions. Allegations involving Legarda must be weighed against official communications and corporate filings; Cusi’s actions, against departmental records and bank transaction records; and Leviste’s operations, against contractual compliance, capitalization, and monetization records.

Entrepreneurial ambition is no crime. But when private wealth is built partly upon exclusive development rights conferred by the state, the public is owed a full accounting of how those rights were secured, who opened the doors, who profited, and why billions in obligations went unmet.
Where wrongdoing is proven, accountability must follow—regardless of surname, fortune, or public office. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Nobel Committee chair emphasizes human accountability for AI’s potential harms
articles.summary: The Nobel Committee chair says human accountability and the rule of law must keep pace with AI’s growing power

blocks.text: Nobel Committee Chair Jørgen Watne Frydnes at Rappler’s Social Good Summit 2026, Saturday, November 21, 2026
Rappler
The Nobel Committee chair says human accountability and the rule of law must keep pace with AI’s growing power

items: Nobel Committee chair Jørgen Watne Frydnes emphasized the need for accountability among AI developers and governments using AI technologies, especially as these systems evolve faster than regulations can keep up.

He highlighted that responsibility for AI's impact lies with individuals and entities that create, deploy, and profit from these technologies, drawing parallels to historical accountability established during the Nuremberg trials.

Frydnes referenced past Nobel laureates to illustrate that society can challenge harmful technologies like AI, and he affirmed the Nobel Peace Prize's role in raising awareness about the importance of ethical considerations in the face of advancing technology.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Nobel Committee chair Jørgen Watne Frydnes at Rappler’s Social Good Summit 2026, Saturday, November 21, emphasized that, ultimately, people behind AI technologies as well as governments that utilize them must be held accountable if these systems inflict harm.

Already, these artificial intelligence systems are developing and moving faster than institutions and laws can respond, the chair said. These technologies are reshaping how people work, how wars are fought, and how societies form opinions.
Algorithms determine what people see while advanced surveillance technologies are giving governments more oppressive ways to monitor journalists, citizens, and activists.
This is a technology that is unique in that it is capable of making a decision for itself. “An atomic bomb could not decide who to bomb. AI can,” Frydnes said.
Frydnes’ attempt to answer the question of how the technology can be shaped for good is rooted in two principles that have routinely surfaced throughout the prize’s history.

First, responsibility should always belong to people. Citing the Nuremberg trials after World War II, he recalled how those established that the responsibility for crimes should always fall on specific individuals and not abstract entities.

“A machine cannot stand before a court, cannot feel remorse, and cannot answer to their victims. But those who design it, own it, deploy it, and profit from their existence, they can, and they should. And so can the states that use them. If we allow technology to become a new abstract entity behind which power hides, we will have undone one of the most important achievements of the last century,” he said.
The second principle is that no one is above the law.

This, he said, “must now also apply to the companies and individuals who hold power over information on a scale that rivals that of many states. A legal order enforced only when it’s politically convenient is no legal order at all.”
Further expounding his point, Frydnes looked to previous laureates, what they represent, and what they mean in the age of AI.
He said the prize’s past offers lessons for understanding the challenges of the present.

Cited were René Cassin, who helped draft the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and received the 1968 Nobel Peace Prize, and Carl von Ossietzky, the German journalist imprisoned in the 1930s by the Nazi regime for exposing its secret rearmament, and more recent laureates such as Maria Ressa and Dmitry Muratov.

He also cited the people behind the Pugwash Conferences who challenged the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction; the International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons, which was recognized in 2017; and 2024 awardee Nihon Hidankyo, the Japanese organization of atomic bomb survivors from Hiroshima and Nagasaki, whose members have spent decades sharing their experiences to prevent the world from forgetting the consequences of nuclear warfare.
These specific awardees are a reminder that artificial intelligence too, is something that society can challenge if it runs counter to the good of humanity.

While Frydnes acknowledged that the Nobel Peace Prize cannot regulate artificial intelligence or independently protect journalists from threats and intimidation, what it can do, he said, is to direct the world’s attention toward people who demonstrate that humanity can confront forces that appear greater than itself.
Frydnes offered a promise of his own, on behalf of those who continue to defend these principles: “We will not duck.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: Yukon power infrastructure project now at Carney's Major Projects Office
articles.summary: On Thursday evening, Prime Minister Mark Carney announced he would be referring the Whitehorse Power Centres project to the Major Projects Office. The project, which will see a federal investment of…

image.caption: Prime Minister Mark Carney and Yukon Premier Currie Dixon shake hands during a meeting on Thursday. After the meeting, Carney announced he would be referring the Whitehorse Power Centres project to the Major Projects Office. (Virginie Ann/CBC)

blocks.text: North·New

On Thursday evening, Prime Minister Mark Carney announced he would be referring the Whitehorse Power Centres project to the Major Projects Office. The project, which will see a federal investment of up to $73 million, includes two new thermal power plants, a new electrical substation and transmission infrastructure in Whitehorse.
Feds investing $73M in Whitehorse Power Centres
The number-one item on Yukon Premier Currie Dixon's wishlist has materialized: federal support for a major power infrastructure project in the territory.
Prime Minister Mark Carney announced Thursday the Whitehorse Power Centres project has been referred to the federal Major Projects Office.

The announcement came after a day of meetings between the prime minister, Yukon Premier Currie Dixon and First Nations leaders in Whitehorse. Before the visit, Dixon said his top priority was talking with Carney about the territory's electrical grid.

"The Yukon is growing, and reliable, affordable electricity is essential to building our future," Dixon said in a news release Thursday night. He added federal support gives the Yukon a chance to double its electricity grid.

items: What will the federal government's Major Projects Office do — and will it succeed?

blocks.text: The Whitehorse Power Centres project, which will now see a federal investment of up to $73 million, includes two new thermal power plants, a new electrical substation and transmission infrastructure in Whitehorse. It will add 15 megawatts of capacity to the grid by 2028, a number that should eventually expand to 150 megawatts in later phases of the project.
A news release from the Prime Minister's Office states the Major Projects Office will help Yukon assess necessary upgrades to accommodate stress on its power grids as a result of the project.
It said the office will also look at opportunities for Indigenous partners to participate in the energy sector, including through potential equity ownership.

Yukon Energy has said the plants are a necessity right now as the grid is under increasing strain. Last winter, the territory almost maxed out its power capacity during a particularly nasty cold snap, prompting warnings from officials of possible rolling blackouts — though it never actually came to that.

This winter, the territory and City of Whitehorse have said they have a plan to prevent that risk from happening again, by selecting buildings to temporarily disconnect from the grid at times of peak energy demand.

The power project in question was identified in the federal budget earlier this month, but Thursday is the first time the federal government has released a figure for how much funding it intends to apply to it.

The Major Projects Office was established to speed up permitting for projects considered to be in the national interest. Other northern projects include the Mackenzie Valley Highway and Taltson hydro expansion in the N.W.T., and the Grays Bay Port and Road Project in Nunavut.

articles.title: Proposed coffee tax 'already dead, buried' --Quimbo
articles.summary: Any proposal that will impose a tax on coffee products is "dead for good," according to House ways and means panel chair Miro Quimbo of Marikina said.

blocks.text: Published November 27, 2026 12:35pm
Any proposal that will impose a tax on coffee products is "dead for good," according to House ways and means panel chair Miro Quimbo of Marikina said.
“Two days ago, dead on arrival po ‘yan. Pero ngayon po, hindi na po pinaglalamayan. Patay na po. Nailibing na po,” Quimbo said in an interview on Super Radyo DZBB
(It was dead on arrival two days ago. Now, there’s no wake. That’s dead and buried.)
Quimbo was responding to the proposal put forward by Olivia Limpe-Aw, Distilled Spirits Association of the Philippines (DSAP) president.
“Marami pong mapipinsala diyan, hindi lang iyong mga coffee farmers natin, pero pati iyong small coffee shops. Starbucks is not the only coffee shop,” Quimbo added.
(That would be devastating not just for coffee farmers, but also for small-time coffee shops.)
Quimbo said his committee is going after increased taxes on alcopops, which are flavored liquor laced with hard drinks such as rhum, margarita, and gin, but with an alcohol content of just 8%.
Tax rates on alcopops, Quimbo said, are way lower than beer due to alcohol content since it contains distilled spirits which are taxed higher.

Quimbo said alcopops should be taxed for what it is, a distilled spirit, and to discourage young people from drinking it because studies have shown that a person picking up a drinking habit early are likely to drink in their lifetime 35% of the time.
“While the alcohol content is just at 8%, those are hard drinks [in it]. That’s distilled sprits which are different from beer, and yet it is taxed lower than beer,” Quimbo said.
“We need to a separate category for alcopops for it to be taxed appropriately. Otherwise, people will just turn to alcopops and that would be more damaging to the health of our people,” Quimbo added.
Tax for airplanes, helicopters
Likewise, Quimbo said that taxes for the wealthy should come from the items they purchase, such as airplanes, helicopters, and luxury vehicles.
The wealth of the most wealthy, Quimbo said, could also come from dividends of the companies where they hold shares, and the value of such shares could also increase over time.
“We are targeting their consumption pattern. Di kayo siguro maniniwala, pero wala pong excise tax ang helicopter, speedboat, jetski. Papatawan po natin ng excise tax po ‘yan,” Quimbo said.
“Some would say that [kind of tax] will only give us a small amount to collect. But that collection still counts,” Quimbo added.
Quimbo said that as it is. taxes for luxury vehicles are just at 50% of the landed cost or the selling price of the dealer, provided that the cost is over P4 million.

“We are proposing to peg the tax at 75% of the actual selling price, and that includes those motorcycles which engines are high powered. If you have a motorcycle at 1000 cc [which cost over P665,000 a unit], sigurado tayo na ang gumagamit nito ay talagang mayayaman,” Quimbo said.
“Again, we need to target the wealth tax at their consumption behavior,” he added. —Llanesca Panti/ VAL, GMA News

articles.title: PH: China has no right, moral basis to dictate whom we will cooperate with
articles.summary: China has neither the right nor moral basis to dictate how and with whom the Philippines will cooperate to defend its sovereignty and national interests, the Department of National Defense said…

blocks.text: Published November 27, 2026 12:14pm

China has neither the right nor moral basis to dictate how and with whom the Philippines will cooperate to defend its sovereignty and national interests, the Department of National Defense said Friday.

DND spokesperson Assistant Secretary Arsenio Andolong issued the statement after China's defense ministry spokesperson Chen Xi called out Japan and Australia for having defense agreements with the Philippines.
"We do not need Beijing’s permission regarding our relations with other nations, especially on matters of our defense and security," Andolong said.

"China's deceptive accusations against other countries of escalating tensions have gone too far, while it continues to use coercion, intimidation, and force to assert its illegal claims in the West Philippine Sea and other waters," he added.

The Defense official said if China truly desires peace and stability in the region, it must cease its intimidation and respect the maritime rights of other nations in accordance with international law, particularly the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).
PH-Japan
In a press briefing Thursday, Chen urged Japan to stop "stirring up trouble" over the South China Sea.

Chen was responding to questions over announcements earlier this month that Japan will provide the Philippines with radars and drones to boost its coastal surveillance capabilities in the latest sign of deepening defense ties between Manila and Tokyo, both formal U.S. military allies.
PH-Australia

China also denounced a defense pact between Australia and the Philippines, arguing it would "exacerbate tensions" in a region crisscrossed by competing territorial claims and vowing to "safeguard" its rights.
The agreement between Canberra and Manila, struck this month during a visit to the Philippine capital by Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, updates a decades-old memorandum.
The countries have steadily increased defense cooperation in recent years, including joint maritime patrols in the strategically vital South China Sea.

Beijing claims most of the South China Sea despite an international ruling that its assertion has no legal basis. US ally the Philippines has been engaged in years of confrontations with China over disputed areas of the waterway.

"Certain Philippine politicians, driven by their selfish interests, are spreading false narratives about China, constantly engaging in provocations and stirring up trouble," Chen told a news conference on Thursday when asked about the deal.
Those individuals are "attempting to enlist the backing of forces from outside the region to embolden themselves and create disturbances in the South China Sea", he said.
"This will only exacerbate tensions and undermine regional stability."

If faced with infringements or provocations, China will "take necessary measures to respond firmly", Chen warned, in order to "resolutely thwart any attempts to plunge the South China Sea into chaos".

The defense deal between Australia and the Philippines involves enhanced maritime activities, sharing of information and defense infrastructure development as key elements, according to Canberra.—with a report from Agence France Presse/AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Duterte’s ICC trial: How to watch and follow the proceedings
articles.summary: Former president Rodrigo Duterte's trial at the International Criminal Court begins on November 30, 2026. Here's how you can follow Rappler's coverage.

blocks.text: DUTERTE. Families of victims of the war on drugs under former president Rodrigo Duterte, along with human rights advocates, gather at the National Council of Churches in the Philippines in Quezon City on September 16, 2026, to watch the live stream of the International Criminal Court’s third status conference.
Jire Carreon/Rappler
Former president Rodrigo Duterte's trial at the International Criminal Court begins on November 30, 2026. Here's how you can follow Rappler's coverage.

MANILA, Philippines – Former Philippine president Rodrigo Duterte will finally face trial before the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague, Netherlands after years of calls for accountability over his violent war on drugs.

The proceedings that will start on Monday, November 30, will put Duterte’s bloody anti-drug campaign under scrutiny. The charges cover alleged killings carried out by the Davao Death Squad when he was mayor of Davao City and those linked to his national drug war during his presidency.
Duterte has been detained at the ICC detention center since his arrest in Manila in March 2025.
Hearings for 2026 are scheduled to run until December 17 before the court’s winter recess. Proceedings will resume on January 11, 2027.

Rappler justice reporter Jairo Bolledo and correspondent Michelle Abad will be in The Hague to cover the trial. They will bring updates from the courtroom and report on activities outside the court and detention center.
Here are the ways to follow Rappler’s coverage and stay on top of the latest developments:

The trial will raise questions about accountability and justice that deserve careful discussion. Join Rappler’s Justice and Crime community to follow the latest developments and exchange views with other readers.

Through the Rappler app you can get notifications and real-time updates. You can also join conversations with Rappler reporters and members of the community. The app is free to download from the Apple App Store and Google Play Store.
Watch Rappler’s livestream of the trial and follow the proceedings as they happen. Our team in The Hague will also share video reports from the court and its surroundings.
For Filipinos following the case from home, the time difference will mean evening viewing. The opening sessions are scheduled to start at 10 am in The Hague or 5 pm in the Philippines.
It is important to remember, though, that the ICC livestream has a 30-minute delay. This means online viewers will see the proceedings begin at 5:30 pm Philippine time.

articles.title: Dutch groups ask court to halt Meta smart glasses sales over privacy concerns
articles.summary: Dutch rights groups argue the glasses developed by Meta and EssilorLuxottica both violate privacy laws and force people to constantly worry in public places, with a chilling effect on society

blocks.text: META SMART GLASSES. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg presents the new line of smart glasses during the Meta Connect event at the company's headquarters in Menlo Park, California, USA, September 23, 2026.
Carlos Barria/Reuters
Dutch rights groups argue the glasses developed by Meta and EssilorLuxottica both violate privacy laws and force people to constantly worry in public places, with a chilling effect on society

items: Dutch consumer and digital rights groups have filed a lawsuit to halt the sales of Meta's AI-powered smart glasses, claiming they violate European privacy laws by enabling covert recordings.

The plaintiffs seek a court ruling to prevent the glasses from being used for unauthorized recordings and to impose penalties for non-compliance, while Meta argues the lawsuit could harm legitimate users and denies any misuse of recorded images.

The backlash against smart glasses is growing globally, with various countries proposing restrictions and legal actions due to privacy concerns, prompting warnings from regulatory bodies about the potential risks associated with such devices.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

AMSTERDAM, The Netherlands – Dutch consumer and digital rights groups asked a court on Thursday, November 26, to halt sales of Meta AI-powered smart glasses in the Netherlands, arguing they violate European privacy laws by allowing wearers to film people without their knowledge.

While limited in scope to the Netherlands, a summary ruling in the civil suit against Meta at the Amsterdam District Court could set a precedent amid growing public backlash, venue bans and regulatory warnings across the world.
A decision is expected by December 24 at the latest.

The rights groups, which include the Netherlands’ main consumer association Consumentenbond and Offlimits, which campaigns against online sex abuse, argued that the glasses developed by Meta and Ray-Ban owner EssilorLuxottica both violate privacy laws and force people to constantly worry in public places, with a chilling effect on society.

The plaintiffs want Meta to prevent its glasses from being used to record people without their knowledge, stop using recordings to train AI models and halt sales until Meta complies. They sought penalties of €100,000 ($109,600) per day per defendant for non-compliance, capped at €100 million.

Offlimits’ lawyer Karlijn Han said the glasses were used for what she described in court as “creep shots.” “Covert recordings are undoubtedly also being made during exams, in changing rooms, at swimming pools, in hotel rooms and hospitals, but also in playgrounds and on beaches,” she said in opening remarks. “Each invasion of privacy is worse than the last.”

Meta’s lawyer Bastiaan Kemp said the court should reject the suit. He said the measures demanded would harm legitimate users, damage Meta’s competitive position and amount to a product recall without resolving concerns about similar devices.

“Providers of products cannot be held responsible for every instance of deliberate misuse,” he told the court. He said that a recording light on the frame makes it obvious when they are being used for recording.

And he denied allegations made by Consumentenbond’s lawyer in court that Meta processes images recorded by the smart glasses in Europe or uses them to train AI models in violation of European law. Meta and manufacturing partner EssilorLuxottica sold more than 7 million smart glasses in 2025, around 80% of the global market.

A lawyer for EssilorLuxottica argued that it neither processes nor has access to footage and that a sales ban would be disproportionate and ineffective given the availability of similar products from other manufacturers.

From proposed restrictions in Australia and Norway to bans in courts across England, Wales, and New York state, governments and judicial authorities are increasingly seeking to prevent covert recording and protect sensitive information. Cinema operators in the UK are also introducing restrictions over privacy and film piracy concerns.

On Tuesday, Germany’s national consumer federation announced legal action against Meta and Ray-Ban over alleged privacy violations, arguing that the glasses make it nearly impossible for consumers to comply with European data protection rules when using them in public.
The European Data Protection Board warned in October that smart glasses raised serious privacy concerns and called for stronger safeguards.

Dutch privacy regulator AP this month advised consumers to not buy smart glasses, saying they are unsafe for both users and bystanders. In October, Dutch retail chain Hans Anders suspended sales of Meta’s ​Ray-Ban smart glasses in the Netherlands and Belgium.
Meta also faces proposed class-action lawsuits in the United States over alleged improper sharing of private images gathered by the glasses. – Rappler.com

articles.title: For a mother who lost 2 sons, Duterte’s ICC trial is a birthday gift
articles.summary: 'My only wish is not just justice for my children, but for all those killed during the time of Rodrigo Duterte. I hope the killings stop for the next generation,' says Llore Pasco who lost her two…

blocks.text: Llore Pasco holds a banner during a send-off as she prepares to depart for The Hague, Netherlands, to attend former President Rodrigo Duterte's International Criminal Court (ICC) trial, at the National Council of Churches in the Philippines (NCCP) in Quezon City, Philippines, November 26, 2026.

'My only wish is not just justice for my children, but for all those killed during the time of Rodrigo Duterte. I hope the killings stop for the next generation,' says Llore Pasco who lost her two sons to the bloody drug war

items: Llore Pasco, a mother who lost her two sons, is traveling to The Hague for the trial of ex-president Rodrigo Duterte, which coincides with her 73rd birthday.
Duterte faces allegations of crimes against humanity related to thousands of extrajudicial killings during his anti-drug campaign, with the trial expected to last until 2027.
The International Criminal Court's proceedings will test its ability to conduct high-profile trials amid external pressures, including sanctions from the United States.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Llore Pasco, a mother who lost her two sons, is traveling to The Hague to attend the trial of ex-president Rodrigo Duterte that will open on her 73rd birthday. She said she had never imagined she would see Duterte in the dock.
“This is the greatest and most beautiful gift you could give me,” she said hours before boarding a plane to the Netherlands.
“My only wish is not just justice for my children, but for all those killed during the time of Rodrigo Duterte. I hope the killings stop for the next generation.”

blocks.caption: Here’s what to expect at the opening of Rodrigo Duterte’s ICC trial

blocks.text: The former Philippine leader goes on trial at the International Criminal Court on Monday, November 30, for alleged crimes against humanity during a six-year anti-drug campaign in which thousands of people were killed.

“For those who have suffered the most egregious abuses during the war on drugs, this will be a welcome moment in their quest for justice,” said Priya Pillai, an international lawyer who runs the Asia Justice Coalition. It “is a significant moment in Philippine history.”

Duterte, 81, faces allegations relating to 85 murders and two attempted murders from 2011 to 2018, including when he served as the mayor of Davao City and the early years of his presidency. The court’s prosecutors say the victims are only a sample of as many as 30,000 people killed by death squads targeting users and sellers of illegal drugs.

blocks.caption: Rodrigo Duterte at ICC: A cheat sheet on understanding his case, trial

blocks.text: It is one of the highest-profile cases to come before the court in its more than two decades of existence, and the biggest since US President Donald Trump’s administration imposed sanctions that could imperil the court’s ability to function.
If convicted of any of three counts of crimes against humanity, Duterte could face life in prison.
Duterte’s supporters have called for his release. His daughter, Vice President Sara Duterte said on Wednesday that “no foreign court or nation should ever stand above the sovereignty of our country.”

The proceedings will test the court’s ability to conduct a high-profile trial amid an ongoing campaign by the United States to force its closure. Washington has imposed crippling financial sanctions and called on member states to withdraw from the ICC and isolate it.

blocks.caption: What happens to Rodrigo Duterte’s case if ICC is dismantled because of Trump?

blocks.text: The ICC is the world’s sole permanent war crimes tribunal, set up to prosecute individuals accused of war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide when national jurisdictions fail to do so.
Duterte is only the second former national leader to appear before it for crimes allegedly committed while in power, after Laurent Gbagbo of Ivory Coast, who was acquitted in 2019.

Four serving national leaders face ICC arrest warrants: Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Russia’s President Vladimir Putin, Afghanistan’s Taliban leader Hibatullah Akhundzada and Myanmar military leader Min Aung Hlaing.
Duterte will be asked on Monday to enter a plea. Prosecutors will then present opening arguments. His lawyers have told judges he denies the charges.
“There was no state or organizational policy to murder,” they argued in a pre-trial brief. “This is not a crimes against humanity case and, as such, does not belong before this court.”

Despite his lawyers arguing that Duterte was unfit to stand trial because of cognitive decline, judges ordered him to stand trial and attend hearings. Court sessions will be shortened to accommodate his age.
During the trial, which is expected to run well into 2027, more than 500 alleged victims will be represented in court.

Prosecutors have said Duterte created, funded and armed death squads responsible for thousands of extrajudicial killings between 2011 and 2019. Philippine law enforcement agencies acknowledged 6,248 deaths.

In language his lawyers dismissed as mere rhetoric, Duterte told supporters during his 2016 election campaign: “I will do just what I did as mayor. You drug pushers, hold-up men and do-nothings, you better go out. Because I’d kill you.”
In March 2025 Duterte was arrested and taken to The Hague, where he is being held in a detention unit for war crimes suspects within a Dutch prison. – Rappler.com

articles.title: China slams PH-Australia defense pact, calls Japan 'destroyer' of regional peace
articles.summary: China's defense ministry on Thursday, November 26, denounced the Philippines' new defense pact with Australia, a deal it says came about as unnamed Filipino politicians have been courting…

blocks.text: November 27, 2026 | 11:31am

MANILA, Philippines — China's defense ministry on Thursday, November 26, denounced the Philippines' new defense pact with Australia, a deal it says came about as unnamed Filipino politicians have been courting "extra-regional forces" to stir up trouble in the South China Sea.

Ministry spokesperson Senior Colonel Chen Xi, speaking at a regular press briefing in Beijing, also called Japan "a real destroyer of peace and tranquility in the Asia-Pacific" over a Japanese defense think tank's report and Tokyo's plan to give the Philippine military a coastal radar system and surveillance drones.

When asked about the deal, Chen did not directly name Australia in his response, and said instead "relevant extra-regional countries" should "earnestly respect" China's sovereignty and "stop meddling and intervening in the South China Sea issue."

"Certain individual politicians in the Philippines, out of their own selfish interests, have spread false China-related narratives, constantly provoked trouble, and vainly attempted to rope in extra-regional forces to back them up, embolden them, and stir up trouble at sea," Chen said, according to an English translation of his remarks.
"This will only heighten tensions and undermine regional stability," he added.
Manila and Canberra signed a defense cooperation agreement on November 15, that would allow for easier and faster coordination on joint military activities.

Defense Secretary Gibo Teodoro and Australian Ambassador Marc Innes-Brown signed the agreement in Manila on the sidelines of the 49th ASEAN summit, with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese looking on.
Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles said in a statement that its main elements include enhanced maritime activities, information-sharing and the development of defense infrastructure.
"The South China Sea should be a sea of peace, friendship, and cooperation; making trouble and provoking confrontation finds no popular support," Chen said.

Chen added that China's actions to protect its sovereignty and maritime rights were "legitimate and lawful," and that Beijing would "continue to take necessary measures to forcefully respond to infringing and provocative acts."

Australian and Philippine troops already train on each other's territory under a status of forces agreement signed in 2007 that took effect in 2012. The two navies also hold joint patrols in the South China Sea.
China claims almost all of the South China Sea, including waters within the Philippines' exclusive economic zone that Manila calls the West Philippine Sea.
In 2016, an international arbitral tribunal ruled in a case filed by Manila that China's sweeping historic claims had no legal basis. Beijing rejects the ruling.

Beijing has long objected to Manila's security ties with Canberra. In August 2025, ministry spokesperson Zhang Xiaogang accused the Philippines of "courting influence from outside powers" after the two countries held joint drills.
Japan's 'academic cloak'

Chen was also asked about a report published by the research arm of Tokyo's defense ministry that makes the case for why Japan must maintain its presence in the South China Sea and keep its ties with regional allies.
In his response, Chen accused Tokyo of using research as cover to justify interfering in the tense waterways.
The China Security Report 2027 was released on November 13 by the National Institute for Defense Studies, the research arm of Japan's Ministry of Defense.

The report says China is building up its ability to operate far from its shores and places high priority on controlling the South China Sea, with an eye to blocking US intervention if it uses force against Taiwan.

It says that if China could blockade the Bashi Channel, the waterway between Taiwan and the Philippines' Batanes islands, and secure air and sea superiority south of Taiwan, its forces could attack southern Taiwan from the South China Sea.

"In order to oppose any unilateral attempt by China to alter the status quo through force or coercion, prevent China from acting even more boldly, and uphold the rule of law and freedom of navigation, it remains essential for Japan to maintain a presence in the South China Sea," a portion of the report's conclusion reads.
NIDS says in the report's preface that the views are the authors' own and do not represent those of the Japanese government, the Ministry of Defense or the institute.
"Draped in an 'academic' cloak, this report by the Japanese side blatantly creates a pretext for its interference in the South China Sea issue and stirring up the Asia-Pacific situation," Chen said.

On November 9, Japanese Ambassador Katsuro Kitagawa and Foreign Affairs Secretary Lazaro signed a 4.3-billion-yen (about $27 million) grant in Manila under Japan's Official Security Assistance program. This assistance includes the provision of coastal radar systems for the Philippine Navy and drones to the Philippine Air Force.
Tokyo says the radar will be the first complete defense system it has supplied under OSA, which it launched in 2023 to provide equipment to the armed forces of partner countries.
Japan's foreign ministry said the equipment would also help protect sea lanes important to Japan, including the South China Sea and the Luzon Strait.

Chen reacted to this by accusing Japan of using a "so-called 'external threat'" as a pretext to stoke security anxieties among its neighbors, transferring weapons and equipment to countries "including the Philippines," and forming exclusive "military cliques."
"Japan is not a party directly concerned in the South China Sea issue and has no right to make irresponsible remarks on it," he said.

articles.title: Heatwaves, floods, fires and rain: weekend of weather extremes expected across Australia
articles.summary:
As bushfires ravage Flinders Island, Victorians can expect a wet and windy election day as storms forecast on east coast

  • Get our

blocks.text: Major fires are among a multitude of weather extremes forecast across Australia on Friday and into the weekend, which also includes severe storms, heavy rain, floods and heatwaves.

Firefighters contending with an out-of-control bushfire on Flinders Island expected conditions to deteriorate further on Friday, as authorities confirmed at least eight buildings had been destroyed or significantly damaged.
The northern deputy regional chief of the Tasmania fire service, Steve Richardson, said: “It’s going to be fairly hot and dry.
“There won’t be much moisture in the air. It will be fairly dry, but the wind could be 20 to 30kmh that may have gusting strengths up to 50 to 60kmh.”
TasAlert has issued bushfire advice warnings for several areas in the island’s north.

People in the Leeka, Mount Tanner, Killiecrankie and Mt Killiecrankie recreation areas have been warned to take shelter after it became too late to leave, while residents of Mt Boyes, Carnacs Flat and surrounds were advised not to return, and those in Palana to monitor for changing conditions. An evacuation centre is open at the Furneaux Arts and Entertainment Centre.
Richardson said it was “unfortunate” that some residents had chosen to remain in Killiecrankie “against all the advice”.
“They’re gambling with their own lives,” he said. “We can’t guarantee that we can get firefighters in to help protect them or protect their property.”

While rain was heading towards Tasmania late on Friday, the Bureau of Meteorology’s Sarah Scully said the heaviest falls would probably miss Flinders Island, but the rainband fed by tropical moisture was an evolving situation.
“It’s a bit of a watch this space,” she said.
Scully said heavy falls were expected in northern Tasmania.
Severe weather warnings have been issued, with the potential for six-hourly rainfall totals of 40 to 70mm and the risk of flash flooding early on Saturday morning.
The rain would increase from the north on Friday evening, and extend statewide overnight.
River and creek rises were likely, and flood watches have been issued for the north-west and central coastal rivers, Forth, Mersey, Meander, North Esk, Tamar, Ringarooma and north coastal rivers.
The weather was expected to take “a big turn later today”, which may come as a surprise to “a lot of Tasmanians who would have woken up to a really dry and sunny morning”, Scully said.
Intense rain in Victoria for polling day

On Friday afternoon, rain was already beginning to fall across Victoria, where a severe weather warning has been issued for heavy rainfall and damaging winds, stretching from the south-west to the north-east. The atmosphere was “laden with moisture” that was ready to come down, Scully said.
Six hourly rainfall totals of 55 to 70mm were likely, with isolated falls up to 110mm possible, and damaging winds with gusts up to 100km/h expected to develop in the north-east on Saturday morning.
after newsletter promotion
On Friday morning, some parts of the Mallee and Wimmera had already received a month’s worth of rain in about an hour, Scully said.
Yaapeet, a town of about 75 people in western Victoria, received 63mm in six hours, including about 36mm in just one hour.
“To give you an idea how heavy that is, when you look at other nearby locations through that region the monthly rainfall is expected to be less than 30mm,” Scully said.
Flash flooding could occur across the central ranges and Otways, with flood watches in place across the north-west, central and north-east catchments, including for the Yarra and Bunyip rivers.
Victorians voting on Saturday could expect conditions to ease from mid-to-late morning, although there was still the potential for showers and storms, Scully said.

To the east, storms with the potential for heavy rain, damaging winds and large hail, could affect areas stretching from southern Queensland to northern and central NSW, including Canberra and Sydney, on Saturday.
By Sunday, the rain band and thunderstorms would begin to shift into north-east New South Wales and south-east Queensland, including parts of Brisbane.
Heatwaves in the north and west

Prolonged heatwave conditions across northern Australia were expected to intensify to severe to extreme levels across northern Western Australia, with temperatures reaching into the mid-40s in the Kimberley.
Perth could see lower intensity heatwave conditions developing over the weekend, and temperatures reaching into the high 30s.
Global heating, driven mainly by the burning of fossil fuels, has increased the frequency and severity of extreme weather events, including heatwaves and bushfires.

articles.title: Judiciary's P84.1-billion proposed budget breezes through Senate
articles.summary: The Senate on Friday quickly approved the P84.1-billion proposed budget of the Judicial branch without any questions asked.

blocks.text: Published November 27, 2026 11:13am
The Senate on Friday quickly approved the P84.1-billion proposed budget of the Judicial branch without any questions asked.

Senator Francis Pangilinan, the budget sponsor in the Upper Chamber, presented the proposed funding of the Supreme Court (SC) and lower courts, Court of Appeals (CA), the Sandiganbayan, the Court of Tax Appeals, and the Presidential Electoral Tribunal.

"Pondohan natin nang buo ang budget na ito. Igalang natin ang fiscal autonomy ng Hudikatura at bigyan natin ang sambayanan ng isang sistemang pangkatarungang nararapat sa tiwala nating lahat," Pangilinan said in his opening statement.
(Let us fully fund this budget. Let us respect the Judiciary's fiscal autonomy and give the country a system that is just and worthy of our trust.)
Backlog of cases
Pangilinan said 98,633 cases were pending for five years in first- and second-level courts as of August 2026, while 49,475 have been pending for 10 years.

The court has taken steps to address this backlog, with the Revised Guidelines for Continuous Trial of Criminal Cases mandating that trying cases under regular cases should not surpass 180 days from the first trial date.

The SC has a P71.702-billion budget, the CA has P7.414 billion, the Sandiganbayan has P3.517 billion, the Court of Tax Appeals has P1.320 billion, and the Presidential Electoral Tribunal has P179.78 billion.
This is the first judiciary budget under the newly installed SC Chief Justice Rodil Zalameda, who assumed his position earlier in November.
With no senator lining up to question the budget, Senator Risa Hontiveros moved to have the Judiciary budget deemed submitted.

"Mister President, there being no reservations for interpellation, I move to close the period of interpellation of the budget of the judiciary, including the Supreme Court of the Philippines and the lower courts, Presidential Electoral Tribunal, Sandiganbayan, the Court of Appeals and the Court of Tax Appeals and that the same be deemed submitted for the body's consideration," Hontiveros said.

"Is there any objection? Hearing none, the period of interpellation for the budget of the Supreme Court and all of its offices is hereby closed and deemed submitted," Senate President Win Gatchalian said. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: New Zealand election ends in hung parliament
articles.summary: A final vote count showed that neither the center-right bloc nor the opposition left bloc was able to secure a majority.

image.caption: Incumbent Prime Minister Christopher Luxon will have to enter negotiations with the Opportunity Party to form the next government [Photo: November 2026]Image: David Rowland/REUTERS

blocks.text: The final vote in New Zealand's election showed on Friday that neither the ruling conservatives nor the opposition bloc has enough seats to form a majority government.
The incumbent three-way coalition government is led by Prime Minister Christopher Luxon of the center-right National Party.
He governed with two other smaller right parties. The incumbent coalition government won 65 seats, two down from election night, final results show.
The left-wing opposition bloc, led by the Labour Party's Chris Hipkins, won 58 seats, up by one from election night.
In terms of vote share of each of the main parties, Luxon's center-right National Party secured 40 seats, while Hipkins main center-left Labour Party won 36 seats.
The official vote count was released after election authorities counted 400,000 so-called special votes.
Those include ballots cast by New Zealanders living abroad.

blocks.caption: Voters delivered a stinging rebuke with the result to the two parties, National and Labour, that have dominated elections in the country [Photo: November 7, 2026]Image: Hollie Adams/REUTERS

blocks.text: Opportunity Party to play kingmaker role in formation of next government

Preliminary results from the November 7 election showed that the ruling coalition held a slim, two-seat majority — that's now been adjusted to the coalition falling short of a majority by a single seat.
The figures leave a new entrant to parliament, the Opportunity Party, as having a preeminent position because it will decide the shape of the next government.

The leader of the centrist party, Qiulae Wong, a 38-year-old former business consultant and a political newcomer, has said earlier this month that she was willing to speak with either party to form a government.
Luxon says negotiations with Opportunity Party will take time
Luxon will have to negotiate with the Opportunity Party if he wants to form the next government.
He said those negotiations will be "challenging" and will take time.
"I want to be upfront with New Zealanders. These negotiations may be challenging, and they could take some time," he told journalists.
"But getting it right matters far more than getting it done quickly. New Zealanders need a government that is stable, that works together, and will last for the full term," he added.
Experts say that if Luxon is not able to form a government with Opportunity, then New Zealanders will have to return to the polls for a new election, according to Australia's public broadcaster.

articles.title: ERC orders P1.98-billion refund for Meralco customers
articles.summary: Over the refund period, a typical household consuming 200 kilowatt-hours monthly will receive a credit of P52 a month.

blocks.text: November 27, 2026 | 11:00am
Linemen install new transformers on an electric post along United Nations Avenue in Manila on March 22, 2026.
The Philippine STAR / Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — Manila Electric Company customers will receive P1.987 billion in refunds over three months after regulators disallowed certain pension and employee benefit expenses passed on to customers and revalued the company’s regulatory asset base.
In a release dated November 26, the Energy Regulatory Commission said that the refund translates to a rate of P0.2611 per kilowatt-hour for residential consumers.
Over the refund period, a typical household consuming 200 kilowatt-hours monthly will receive a credit of P52 a month.
The order follows a rate unbundling dispute dating back to 2003 over how Meralco’s assets and operating expenses should be valued and reflected in customer bills.
Complying with a 2025 Supreme Court ruling, the ERC revised Meralco’s plant value using a new method and finalized the company’s plant value at P67.78 billion in 2026.
The new figure is lower than the nearly P70-billion valuation previously used to determine electricity rates.
As a result of its review, the ERC also disallowed P89.82 million in pension and employee benefit expenses previously passed on to customers.

Though such operating costs may be charged to consumers, the Supreme Court held that these costs must be justified. The commission said that Meralco’s submissions lacked the necessary breakdown of salaries and benefits to establish their reasonableness.
Power companies, however, are not prohibited from offering their employees higher pensions.
Commission Chairman Francis Saturnino Juan told DZBB on Friday, November 27, that the ERC uses minimums and benchmarking to determine what benefit costs may be passed on to consumers.
Expenses that exceed the commission’s decision on rate unbundling must be shouldered by the company.
Other sanctions expected
Juan said that the commission will also follow up with power players in the Visayas and Mindanao that were called to explain recurring plant outages and blackouts.

In November 2026, 13 companies, including affiliates of Meralco subsidiary Meralco PowerGen Corp., were issued show-cause orders over their reported non-compliance with reliability performance standards.
According to Juan, the firms have since submitted their verified explanations to the commission, citing technical issues as the cause of the outage events.

articles.title: [DECODED] How Facebook pages used Kitty’s image to amplify Dutertismo
articles.summary: Rappler’s analysis shows how digital creators and pages masquerading as news sites are using the former president’s youngest daughter as a vehicle to keep Dutertismo alive

blocks.text: Veronica “Kitty” Duterte has become a prominent voice in her family’s public defense of former president Rodrigo Duterte, now detained in The Hague for alleged crimes against humanity. Supporters celebrate her as a devoted daughter, ready to stand by her “Papa Rody.”

Circulating on Facebook is an image that captures this: the 81-year-old Duterte showing concern that he had “embarrassed” his family and Kitty holding his hand, reassuring him that his children remained “proud to be his flesh and blood.” This storyline has spread, feeding into a broader appeal for Duterte loyalty ahead of the 2028 presidential elections.

Rappler analyzed 260 public Facebook posts containing mentions of Kitty, published between January and October 2026, and found at least three clusters of narratives in which accounts shared nearly identical captions. Some accounts spread content across narratives, while others published posts appearing within short intervals of each other. The largest cluster, gaining almost five million views, centered on Kitty’s support for her detained father.

These posts foreground Duterte’s separation from his family, shifting attention away from the allegations of crimes against humanity he faces at the International Criminal Court (ICC). Duterte was arrested in March 2025 in connection with the ICC proceedings concerning killings during his administration’s anti-drug war campaign.
In his absence, Duterte’s children – Paolo, Sara, Sebastian, and Kitty – have taken up the mantle of speaking on his behalf.

The 22-year-old Kitty, Duterte’s youngest daughter with his common-law wife Honeylet Avanceña, especially finds herself at the frontlines. Her interviews and heartfelt posts on social media have supplied material for online accounts aiming to rally sympathy and support for the Dutertes.

Unlike her siblings, Kitty is a fresh face with no political track record to be judged on, which could make her appeal to supporters stronger, Arjan Aguirre, assistant professor of political science at Ateneo de Manila University, told Rappler.

“With Kitty, they’re trying to project the idea to the general public that even if you are not a supporter of the Duterte bloc, you have to sympathize with us because I am the youngest, I’m the bunso, and I feel sad about what’s happening,” according to Aguirre, who is also pursuing his PhD in political science at the University of Pittsburgh.

Kitty was only 14 when her father was elected president in 2016, while her siblings already held local seats in Davao. That distance from politics, Aguirre said, is what makes her the obvious choice to convey these seemingly innocent narratives.

He highlighted that Kitty’s image projects a gentler tone than her siblings. “Nag-bo-border pa rin siya doon sa pagiging naive. May mga persecution pa rin siyang nababanggit pero hindi gano’n katapang.” (She still borders on being naive. She does mention persecution, but not as boldly.)

More than half of the 260 posts analyzed pulled emotionally-charged quotes from Kitty’s interview with blogger Alvin & Tourism on April 20. Posting peaked the following day, April 21, just days before news broke out of the ICC’s confirmation of Duterte’s charges.
The same quotes then resurfaced in September, when Duterte made his first in-person appearance at the ICC courtroom since his arrest.
By October, the posts about the “flesh and blood” narrative had accumulated about 4.76 million views on Facebook, based on Rappler’s monitoring.

Behind those views were 78 pages and profiles that circulated the narrative. Rappler identified 17 pages linked to Pilipinas Today, a network of news and media pages operating across the country. An earlier investigation found that the group is run by Sartine IT Solutions, a political consulting firm previously linked to foreign interference in elections.

Alongside the Pilipinas Today network, some news-branded pages that had previously used partisan names contributed to the narrative’s amplification. For instance, the page News Ngayon – which accounted for 21.67% of the total post views in this cluster – changed its name six times. It was originally Duterte Latest News, when it was created on January 17, 2018.

Another profile, Venielyn Rahman, which categorizes itself as a news and media website, racked up a total of 110,075 views for the same quotes from Kitty on April 21. A closer look at its Profile Transparency information indicated that the primary location of the profile owner is listed in Bangladesh. The account, however, largely published Filipino celebrity content and political news.
It is among the four pages whose administrators are located outside the Philippines, including one based in Macau, one in Canada, and a second one in Bangladesh.

blocks.caption: OUTSIDE THE PHILIPPINES. Four pages had administrators located in other countries. Rappler screenshots

blocks.text: Other pages in this cluster hid their political purpose behind misleading names. The page Words of Wisdom: Inspirational Quotes to Live By, which has about 141,000 followers, claims to be “dedicated to providing you with daily inspiration, motivation, and positivity,” but in fact carries political content about the Dutertes.
In a second cluster of posts, Facebook pages cast Kitty as the messenger of her father’s supposed political support for protests back home, and appeared to cash in on this narrative.

At least 19 Facebook fan pages shared identical captions attributing the message to Kitty, accompanied by carousels that steered users toward the same affiliate marketing link. These pages accumulated more than 21,000 post views as of October.

blocks.caption: REPETITIVE POSTS. Facebook pages analyzed showed identical posts containing affiliate marketing links. Rappler screenshots

blocks.text: Posts spiked a few days after Iglesia ni Cristo’s three-day demonstration from June 30 to July 2 in support of long-time Duterte ally Senator Rodante Marcoleta.

blocks.caption: AFFILIATE LINKS. Facebook pages cast Kitty as the messenger of her father’s supposed political support for protests back home, then added links to an online marketplace. Rappler screenshots

blocks.text: Further inspection of 12 of these pages found similar blue checkmark edits on their profile images, mimicking the verification badges Facebook awards to premium accounts. Some of them also posted the same manipulated photos within minutes of each other.

blocks.caption: FAKE CHECKMARKS. Facebook pages found in Rappler’s dataset showed blue checkmarks edited on their profile photos. Rappler screenshots

blocks.text: For Aguirre, all these narratives position Kitty as a political force – even a potential successor – within the Duterte dynasty.
“If ever Rodrigo Roa Duterte is gone, who would emerge [a]s the central figure in the Duterte bloc? I’m sure Kitty will put up a fight for that,” he added.

The third cluster of posts echoed this push to keep the Duterte legacy alive through his children. Rappler’s analysis found copypasta messages across 29 pages and profiles in January, claiming that only the Dutertes could put an end to crime and corruption.

“Hindi sila basta anak ni Tatay Digong. Sila ang legasiya ng tapang, disiplina, malasakit, at paninindigang walang atrasan—kahit malalakas pa ang kalaban,” the captions read. (They’re not just children of Tatay Digong. They are the legacy of courage, discipline, compassion, and an unwavering resolve—even when facing formidable opponents.)

One post carrying this message, published by the page Parang May Mali, garnered 1.75 million views. The profile Boss Lee Vlog distributed it across seven Facebook groups, including communities of local buying and selling, hog raising, and religious discussion.

By July, the accounts in this cluster began to explicitly push for #Duterte2028. The Facebook page Kitty Duterte: Unofficial wrote, “Kung sunod-sunod na tatakbong pangulo ang mga Duterte, susuportahan mo ba sila?” (If the Dutertes run for president one after another, will you support them?) In the same caption, it answered its own question, “YES NA YES.”

According to Aguirre, 2028 could be the Dutertes’ year. If the vice president gets impeached, he predicted, whoever they field in the polls could win by saying the family had been persecuted and wronged.

These accounts suggest that the campaign has already begun. With Sara’s presidential bid in the works, these accounts have a clear pitch to the Filipino people beyond sympathy for her father: back the next Duterte. – with reports from Alex Culla/Rappler.com

Nica is a freelance journalist and OSINT researcher reporting on online information manipulation campaigns and tech platform accountability. Her work has centered on information integrity, previously fact-checking mis/disinformation and building news products at VERA Files. She is now pursuing a joint master’s degree in Journalism, Media, and Globalization in Europe. You may reach her at ndhanopol@gmail.com.

articles.title: Imee, Robin to Marcos admin: Cease ICC cooperation, return ex-Pres Duterte to PH
articles.summary: Senators Imee Marcos and Robin Padilla have filed a resolution urging the executive branch to immediately cease all cooperation with the International Criminal Court and exhaust all legal and…

blocks.text: Published November 27, 2026 9:47am

Senators Imee Marcos and Robin Padilla have filed a resolution urging the executive branch to immediately cease all cooperation with the International Criminal Court and exhaust all legal and diplomatic means for the release and repatriation of former President Rodrigo Duterte.

In Senate Resolution 797 filed on November 25, Marcos and Padilla also urged the executive branch to discontinue efforts to serve the arrest warrant issued by the ICC against Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa.

They said the Philippines withdrew from the Rome Statute in 2019, terminating its status as a state party. However, despite pronouncements by authorities that the ICC has no jurisdiction in the country, Duterte was arrested and brought to The Hague, Netherlands, where he was turned over to the custody of the international court.
They added that authorities are also undertaking measures to locate, arrest, and turn over Dela Rosa to the ICC.

The senators also cited the joint Heads of State Declaration toward Peace issued by US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping "expressly recognizing that the principles of state consent and respect for the immunities of state officials are of paramount importance and declaring that the ICC and similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction."

"In the exercise of its independent foreign policy, the Philippines must carefully consider significant developments in international relations, particularly when the positions articulated by major international partners bear directly upon matters affecting Philippine sovereignty, national interest, and the rights of Filipino citizens," Marcos and Padilla said.

They further said that the country's continued cooperation with the ICC, particularly in relation to the arrest of Duterte and the enforcement of an arrest warrant against Dela Rosa, must be reassessed.

"The pursuit of justice and accountability must remain consistent with the Constitution, the protection of fundamental rights, and the sovereign right of the Philippines to administer justice through its own institutions, without foreclosing accountability for crimes punishable under Philippine law," they said.
GMA News Online reached out to Malacañang for comment and will publish it once available. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: New Zealand's ruling coalition falls short of parliamentary majority by one seat
articles.summary: The right-leaning ruling bloc led by the National Party has fallen short of the majority needed to govern.

blocks.text: New Zealand's ruling coalition has fallen short of a parliamentary majority by one seat, following a campaign shaped by a sluggish economy and disillusioned voters.
It now needs the support of the centrist Opportunity Party to remain in power. If they cannot reach a deal, the country may have to go back to the polls.
The incumbent National Party led by Prime Minister Christopher Luxon secured 40 out of 130 seats, while its coalition partners ACT and New Zealand First took 13 and 12 respectively.
A government led by the centre-left Labour Party is not possible, official results on Friday show, as the bloc would not have enough seats even if Opportunity threw its weight behind it.
Labour secured 36 seats, The Greens took 17, while Te Pāti Māori, which represents Māori interests, picked up five.

Opportunity, which has been described as this election's kingmaker, secured seven seats. The party's leader Qiulae Wong has previously said she will negotiate first with the party that secures the largest number of seats.
Preliminary results on 7 November, election day, had projected that National combined with its coalition partners would have a slim lead over the left-leaning bloc.
But today's official tally shows it had lost two seats on special votes - cast by citizens who were overseas or outside of their registered electorate on election day - which typically skew left.
Some of National's key election pledges include lower taxes, cheaper energy, more renewable generation, and a greater focus on defence.
Labour, meanwhile, had campaigned to cut healthcare, public transport and fuel costs, more government support for social housing, among other things.

New Zealand's mixed-member proportional voting system means most governments are coalitions. Each voter makes two choices – for the representative of their constituency in parliament and a political party.
In earlier interviews with the BBC, many voters had expressed frustration over spiralling costs of living and high unemployment across the country, with declining faith in their political leadership.
"There's this kind of apathy and a bit of dread," said 21-year-old Imogen Vlutger.
A 40-year-old man said he didn't vote as he could not bring himself to tick any of the boxes on the ballot paper.
More than half of the country no longer see New Zealand as a land of opportunity, according to a survey by the Helen Clark Foundation, a public policy think tank.
Kiwis have been leaving the country in record numbers, with many of them, including former prime minister Jacinda Arden, moving to Australia.

articles.title: Families of slain Filipinos seek justice as Duterte's ICC trial set to start
articles.summary: Former Philippine leader Rodrigo Duterte goes on trial at the International Criminal Court on Monday for alleged crimes against humanity during a six-year anti-drug campaign in which thousands of…

blocks.text: Published November 27, 2026 9:26am

Former Philippine leader Rodrigo Duterte goes on trial at the International Criminal Court on Monday for alleged crimes against humanity during a six-year anti-drug campaign in which thousands of people were killed.

Duterte, 81, faces allegations relating to 85 murders and 2 attempted murders from 2011 to 2018, including when he served as the mayor of Davao City and the early years of his presidency. The court's prosecutors say the victims are only a sample of as many as 30,000 people killed by death squads targeting users and sellers of illegal drugs.

It is one of the highest-profile cases to come before the court in its more than two decades of existence, and the biggest since US President Donald Trump's administration imposed sanctions that could imperil the court's ability to function.
If convicted of any of three counts of crimes against humanity, Duterte could face life in prison.
Llore Pasco, a mother who lost her two sons, is travelling to The Hague to attend the trial that will open on her 73rd birthday. She said she had never imagined she would see Duterte in the dock.
"This is the greatest and most beautiful gift you could give me," she said hours before boarding a plane to the Netherlands.
"My only wish is not just justice for my children, but for all those killed during the time of Rodrigo Duterte. I hope the killings stop for the next generation."

Duterte’s supporters have called for his release. His daughter Sara Duterte, now serving as Philippine vice president, said in a statement on Wednesday that "no foreign court or nation should ever stand above the sovereignty of our country."

blocks.caption: On 13 October 2026, Trial Chamber III of the International Criminal Court (ICC) held a fourth status conference in the case of The Prosecutor v. Rodrigo Roa Duterte. Trial Chamber III is composed of Presiding Judge Joanna Korner, Judge Keebong Paek and Judge Nicolas Guillou. (c)ICC-CPI

blocks.text: On 13 October 2026, Trial Chamber III of the International Criminal Court (ICC) held a fourth status conference in the case of The Prosecutor v. Rodrigo Roa Duterte. Trial Chamber III is composed of Presiding Judge Joanna Korner, Judge Keebong Paek and Judge Nicolas Guillou. (c)ICC-CPI
TEST OF EMBATTLED ICC

The proceedings will test the court's ability to conduct a high-profile trial amid an ongoing campaign by the United States to force its closure. Washington has imposed crippling financial sanctions and called on member states to withdraw from the ICC and isolate it.
The ICC is the world's sole permanent war crimes tribunal, set up to prosecute individuals accused of war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide when national jurisdictions fail to do so.
Duterte is only the second former national leader to appear before it for crimes allegedly committed while in power, after Laurent Gbagbo of Ivory Coast, who was acquitted in 2019.

Four serving national leaders face ICC arrest warrants: Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Russia's President Vladimir Putin, Afghanistan's Taliban leader Hibatullah Akhundzada and Myanmar military leader Min Aung Hlaing.
Duterte will be asked on Monday to enter a plea. Prosecutors will then present opening arguments. His lawyers have told judges he denies the charges.
"There was no state or organisational policy to murder," they argued in a pre-trial brief. "This is not a crimes against humanity case and, as such, does not belong before this court."

blocks.caption: Families of victims of the drug war killings and rights violations under the Duterte regime, lawyers, church people, and rights advocates hold a group watch on the International Criminal Court (ICC) status conference in the case of former President Rodrigo Duterte at the Function Room, National C…

blocks.text: Families of victims of the drug war killings and rights violations under the Duterte regime, lawyers, church people, and rights advocates hold a group watch on the International Criminal Court (ICC) status conference in the case of former President Rodrigo Duterte at the Function Room, National Council of Churches in EDSA, Quezon City September 16, 2026. Photo by Danny Pata
DEATH SQUADS

Despite his lawyers arguing that Duterte was unfit to stand trial because of cognitive decline, judges ordered him to stand trial and attend hearings. Court sessions will be shortened to accommodate his age.
During the trial, which is expected to run well into 2027, more than 500 alleged victims will be represented in court.

Prosecutors have said Duterte created, funded and armed death squads responsible for thousands of extrajudicial killings between 2011 and 2019. Philippine law enforcement agencies acknowledged 6,248 deaths.

In language his lawyers dismissed as mere rhetoric, Duterte told supporters during his 2016 election campaign: "I will do just what I did as mayor. You drug pushers, hold-up men and do-nothings, you better go out. Because I'd kill you."
In March 2025 Duterte was arrested and taken to The Hague, where he is being held in a detention unit for war crimes suspects within a Dutch prison.

"For those who have suffered the most egregious abuses during the war on drugs, this will be a welcome moment in their quest for justice," said Priya Pillai, an international lawyer who runs the Asia Justice Coalition. It "is a significant moment in Philippine history."
